verdict.rationale: Airbyte has several built-in event-driven behaviors. It sends notifications to email or webhook on important events, lets you set per-connection rules for handling source schema changes, and can run dbt Cloud transformations immediately after syncs. These are fixed, predefined triggers rather than a general user-defined rules engine. Cron and interval scheduling are time-based, not event-based, so they do not count here. Missing for 10: a general-purpose event→action rules engine with configurable conditions, documentation of the available event types and actions in depth, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: If you want Airbyte to notify you about important events, use its built-in notification system.
Airbyte can send notifications to an email address, webhook, or both.
You can specify for each connection how Airbyte should handle any change of schema in the source.
By using the dbt Cloud integration, you can create and run dbt transformations immediately following syncs in Airbyte Cloud.
